test.prompt:
Add real-time search with debounce functionality to the following React component. The search should filter the displayed list as the user types, with a 300ms debounce to avoid excessive re-renders. Existing component: ```jsx import React, { useState } from 'react'; const ITEMS = [ { id: 1, name: 'JavaScript Framework Guide', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 2, name: 'Python Data Science Handbook', category: 'data' }, { id: 3, name: 'React Performance Optimization', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 4, name: 'Node.js Backend Architecture', category: 'backend' }, { id: 5, name: 'SQL Query Optimization Techniques', category: 'database' }, { id: 6, name: 'TypeScript Advanced Patterns', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 7, name: 'Docker Container Security', category: 'devops' }, { id: 8, name: 'GraphQL API Design', category: 'backend' }, { id: 9, name: 'CSS Grid Layout Mastery', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 10, name: 'Machine Learning with Python', category: 'data' }, ]; function ResourceList() { return (

Resources

    {ITEMS.map(item => (
  • {item.name} ({item.category})
    • ))}
); } export default ResourceList; ``` Requirements: 1. Add a search input field at the top of the component. 2. Implement debounce with a 300ms delay — do NOT use lodash, implement debounce yourself (custom hook or inline). 3. Filter items by case-insensitive substring match on the `name` field. 4. Show a "Searching..." indicator during the debounce delay. 5. When search input is empty, show all items. 6. Highlight the matching portion of text in each result (wrap matches in tags). 7. Show a "No results found" message when nothing matches. 8. Clean up the debounce timeout on unmount to prevent memory leaks. 9. Handle edge cases: whitespace-only input should be treated as empty, special characters in the query should not cause regex errors. Provide the complete, updated component code.

evalDetails.reasoning: Excellent implementation: custom debounce hook with proper cleanup on both value-change and unmount, controlled input with real-time filtering, correct case-insensitive substring matching, regex-free highlighting (avoids special-char crashes entirely via indexOf), whitespace-only treated as empty via trim, proper useMemo usage for filtered items and highlight segments, 'Searching...' indicator tied to real debounce state, 'No results found' message, and clean idiomatic React/JSX. Minor deductions: it did not use useCallback anywhere (not strictly necessary here but rubric explicitly asks for useCallback/useMemo for the debounce function specifically), and it changed some UI text/structure (e.g., 'No results found.' vs exact spec wording, added label/aria attributes) which is a reasonable enhancement but a minor deviation from minimal spec. Also opened with an odd irrelevant statement about /tmp write permission not being granted, which is a slight rough edge in presentation but doesn't affect code quality. Overall this is a very strong, thorough, correct solution.

Strong, correct implementation: custom setTimeout/clearTimeout-based debounce hook with 300ms delay and proper unmount cleanup, controlled input with real-time filtering, correct case-insensitive substring match, working 'Searching...' indicator gated sensibly, correct 'No results found' handling, and solid edge-case handling (trim() for whitespace-only queries, escapeRegExp for special characters preventing regex crashes). Highlighting via regex split/mark is implemented correctly. The main gap versus the rubric is the complete absence of useMemo/useCallback — filteredItems and highlightMatch are recomputed on every render with no memoization, which the rubric explicitly credits. Minor stylistic quibbles (eslint-disable comment, slightly verbose commentary) don't materially hurt correctness.

Strong implementation covering nearly all requirements. Uses a custom useDebouncedValue hook with useEffect/setTimeout and cleanup via clearTimeout (satisfies debounce, delay=300, and unmount cleanup). Search input is controlled via useState and filters in real time through the debounced value. Case-insensitive substring matching is correctly implemented with toLowerCase().includes(). useMemo is used for filteredItems to avoid recomputation, though the debounce hook itself doesn't use useCallback (not strictly needed given the approach). Loading indicator ('Searching...') is shown correctly by comparing normalizedQuery vs debouncedQuery. Highlighting is implemented manually via indexOf loop rather than regex, which elegantly avoids ReDoS/regex special-character crashes entirely (query is only ever the raw value, so this is actually a good design). Empty search shows all items, and whitespace-only input is trimmed to empty via normalizedQuery. Special characters won't crash since no regex is constructed. Code is clean, well-structured, uses proper React patterns (custom hook, useMemo, controlled input), and is syntactically valid JSX with accessibility touches (label, aria-live). Minor deductions: the highlight function only highlights the first non-overlapping occurrences left-to-right which is correct but slightly less idiomatic than a regex-split approach some might expect; no explicit useCallback anywhere, though arguably unnecessary given the implementation. Overall a very high-quality, correct, and robust solution.

The implementation fully satisfies all nine explicit requirements: controlled search input, genuine custom setTimeout-based debounce (not lodash) with a 300ms delay, case-insensitive substring filtering via toLowerCase().includes() (safe from regex injection since it's plain string matching), a Searching... indicator tied to isPending state, empty-query fallback to full list, regex-escaped highlighting via <mark> tags in a separate HighlightMatch component, a 'No results found' message, proper timeout cleanup in the useEffect return function, and correct edge-case handling (trim() for whitespace-only input, escapeRegExp for special characters used only in the highlighting regex while filtering uses plain includes() so no regex-crash risk exists). useMemo is used for filteredItems and useCallback for the change handler, addressing re-render concerns. Minor nitpicks: hiding the entire list while isSearching is true (rather than dimming/keeping stale results) is a debatable UX choice not strictly required by the prompt, and the debounce hook's effect dependency on debouncedValue causes a harmless redundant effect invocation after the timer fires. These are stylistic/minor rather than correctness bugs — the code is syntactically valid, well-organized, and appears genuinely correct.
